findings.title: UMass Global MyPath BBA current price and applicability need catalog reconciliation
facts: The currently live university tuition page labels its schedule 2025–2026. It quotes $3,500 per 24-week undergraduate MyPath billing period, a minimum of 12 units per billing period and $7,000 per 48-week CBE academic year, and explicitly directs readers to the academic catalog for the latest rates.

The official general-business self-paced marketing page still advertises $3,400 per six-month access period, 120 credits and up to 90 previous college transfer credits. The effective date of the difference was not established. Twenty-four weeks must not be silently equated with six calendar months.
University accreditation page confirms WSCUC institutional accreditation.

The 2025–2026 legacy MyPath catalog requires a minimum of 30 equivalent credits in university residence including LBSC 320 and LBSC 321; accredited transfer coursework must first match credit-hour courses and then competencies, with B- or better. It accepts ACE recommendations subject to degree and residency limits. The newer 2026–2027 consolidated policies were present in repository source references but were not independently retrieved during this audit.
The legacy catalog states M/mastery grades, no university-calculated GPA and a credit-hour conversion record on request. It does not justify a claim of traditional letter grades.

Provider-published Sophia equivalencies already exist in the school kit. They are not a verified MyPath competency map. Existing six credit-hour degree models use different curricula and must not receive MyPath subscription rules.

transfer.scope: Advertised prior college coursework, subject to BBA applicability

assessment.note: No official current program-specific guarantee of non-proctored BBA assessment found.

blockers: Current 2026–2027 catalog tuition and fee schedule not independently retrieved.
Current consolidated MyPath policy and residency rules not independently verified.
No 60+ applicable semester-equivalent credit MyPath competency allocation verified; no independent numeric ACE cap.
No current course-specific assessment/proctoring evidence.
findings.proposedAction: Keep the published FY2025–26 quote and $3,400 marketing discrepancy explicit; current-rate confidence unknown. Preserve historical data and current credit-hour mappings; do not promote a new MyPath degree plan by title matching.

findings.title: Purdue Global ExcelTrack BSBA term cost and native quarter-credit requirements

scope.award: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration

costs.exclusions: Other course-specific fees and personal costs not independently verified

facts: Official BSBA marketing states 174 single-credit courses plus a six-quarter-credit capstone, totaling 180 quarter credits.
The catalog degree plan totals 45 core, 83 major and 52 open-elective quarter credits. MT499 is the six-quarter-credit capstone.

General prior-learning rules permit at most 75% externally assessed undergraduate prior learning and exclude program capstones. For this 180-quarter-credit degree that is a computed ceiling of 135 quarter credits, leaving at least 45 quarter credits outside the externally assessed category. It is not a guarantee of 135 applicable ACE quarter credits.
Internal Purdue Assessment of Skills and Knowledge credits marked AC can count as residency. Do not describe all 45 remaining credits as conventional taught courses.

The existing Sophia school kit uses original-source semester quantities and receiving quarter-credit awards. A 4.5-quarter-credit award must not be inflated to match a native five-quarter-credit course.

transfer.residencyRemainderBasis: Calculated from external prior-learning ceiling; internally assessed credits may count

blockers: No complete 90+ applicable quarter-credit external credit allocation established.
No program-specific guaranteed ACE maximum or complete assessment/proctoring matrix.
Native course prerequisite and module sequencing ledger not fully extracted; no new degree model recommended.
findings.proposedAction: Use verified cost/quarter-credit facts in editorial. Root audit found no listed Purdue degree to withdraw. Keep new academic pathway held until exact degree-applicable award balances and requirements are supported.

findings.title: Professional Studies independent subscription closed to new enrollments and reentries

scope.award: Bachelor of Science in Professional Studies

facts: The current 2026–2027 catalog states: Effective July 1, 2026, the independent model will no longer be accepting enrollments or reentries.

Published independent-model prices remain $195 per month plus $100 for each Assessment of Skills and Knowledge and $2,226 for the bachelor PR499 capstone. Capstone tuition is billed in addition to the monthly subscription during enrollment in the course.
A term-based Professional Studies version also exists; independent subscription prices must not be attached to that version.

The BSPr requires 180 quarter credits and a final traditional six-quarter-credit PR499 capstone. Four professional competency tutorials are required; ASK attempts are capped at two per assessment; the independent model requires 10 quarter credits each 12 months.

The catalog allows requirements other than the capstone to be fulfilled via prior learning, subject to applicable university rules. This wording does not override the generic externally assessed cap or prove degree applicability.

costs.eligibility: Continuing eligible independent-model students; closed to new enrollments and reentries effective 2026-07-01

blockers: Continuing-student individual eligibility requires the university's decision.
No academic mappings were created; new-student independent pathway must remain unavailable.
findings.proposedAction: Lead editorial with closure and scope subscription cost to eligible continuers. Preserve historical student records. No current program-catalog Purdue entry exists to remove.

findings.title: South College generic transfer pages conflict; graduate CBE cannot inherit undergraduate caps
facts: The official transfer-information page states a 75% ceiling for credits earned at other institutions; the official academics page states 60%.
The transfer-information page explicitly says Sophia Learning and StraighterLine courses are not accepted. A generic college-course cap cannot be represented as an ACE allowance.
Graduate policies are set by associated program faculty. Existing CBE inventory contains graduate degrees, so neither undergraduate figure establishes a graduate CBE allowance.
blockers: Effective date and controlling undergraduate catalog policy unresolved.
Exact graduate CBE program transfer limits, applicable credit and assessment constraints unresolved.
Accreditation not independently checked in this subtask, so no recommendation.
findings.proposedAction: Retain conflict in watchlist; do not set a universal CBE cap.

findings.title: CBU online $541/unit and 100-unit advertising require residency reconciliation
facts: The online BA Business Administration (Management) page advertises $541 plus fees per unit, 48 major units, eight-week sessions and a 16-month estimate conditional on prior general education and electives.

Multiple current online program FAQs advertise a maximum of 100 transferred units. The repository's already retained online undergraduate transfer policy instead requires 36 CBU residence units including 30 upper-division units.
The 48-unit major listing is not the total bachelor's degree. No 100-unit applicable bachelor allocation, current catalog reconciliation or ACE policy was established.

findings.title: Memphis/Saylor partnership does not establish a new mapped degree plan

The university College of Arts and Sciences advising FAQ explicitly says Saylor and other alternative transfer sources do not count toward university residency. CAS major/minor residence requires regular letter-grade class enrollment (six major and three minor semester hours).
This is not evidence Saylor itself awards traditional university letter grades or that any specific 10–20 courses apply to a residential degree.

Institutional accreditation and at least 50% applicable degree transfer not independently checked here.

findings.title: National University Sophia partnership is established; degree applicability still controls
facts: NU's current Credit for Prior Learning page names Sophia Learning and StraighterLine as alternative course providers whose college-level courses may transfer.
NU's testing services page lists Sophia equivalencies. Generic partner status does not prove that 50% of a particular NU degree can be supplied by Sophia or establish a uniform ACE cap.
NU quarter-credit award quantities must retain their native unit and must not be silently equated with Sophia semester credits.
blockers: No new exact degree-level course plan or current institutional accreditation verification in this subtask.
findings.proposedAction: No duplicate partnership feature needed; existing NU kit remains scoped and new degree applicability stays held.

findings.title: RMCAD/Sophia partner table verified with program-dependent alternatives
facts: The provider's RMCAD partner page says RMCAD teamed up with Sophia and provides a specific transfer table.

Examples include English Composition I to EN1110 and English Composition II to EN1111, each three provider credits; other rows offer several elective alternatives. These are provider-published matches and are not an additive degree allocation.
The page says Sophia courses are pass/fail and advises checking applicability with the school. It is not a traditional letter-grade online-to-campus route.
blockers: RMCAD degree total, residence/ACE caps, institutional accreditation and at least50% applicable transfer not independently verified.
No 10–20 nonduplicative applicable course allocation established.
findings.proposedAction: Retain partnership evidence; no new mapped degree recommendation.

findings.title: WGU ACE restrictions are program-specific; no universal new rule established
facts: Official WGU pathway pages explicitly identify a named program/catalog and provider. They state at least25% of undergraduate competency units must be completed through residency and courses may not satisfy multiple courses of study.

The May2026 Sophia BS Supply Chain and Operations Management preview shows55 potential transfer CUs of110required, but duplicate parser rows and preview status mean this is not a newly approved pathway ledger.
Other WGU pathways list different potential totals; no university-wide ban or uniform degree-level ACE limit was established. Graduate and undergraduate rules must remain separate.
WGU competency units are preserved as CUs; no silent credit-unit conversion is authorized.
blockers: No specific alleged new restriction/effective date established.
Exact receiving-program table needs current source capture and applicability validation before modification.
findings.proposedAction: Keep existing exact program rules and historical valid awards; do not apply a generic restriction.

findings.title: Online-to-residential 10–20 course and traditional letter-grade pathway exploration
facts: ASU Universal Learner primary evidence supplied by the baseline-provider research agent says posted courses appear on an official ASU transcript identically to on-campus/online courses. ENG101 is three hours of first-year composition; CAP150 is a three-hour elective.
The same agent verified admissions restrictions for currently admitted ASU degree-seeking students and minimum posting timelines; this is not an unrestricted accelerator for any enrolled student.

Neither that evidence nor this subtask establishes a destination-specific set of10–20 applicable courses, traditional A/B/C transcript proof for the proposed route, or at least50% applicable transfer capacity.
Provider pass/fail credit at Sophia/RMCAD and mastery transcripts at MyPath do not become traditional letter grades through a partnership.

sources.retrieval: Agent-provided primary evidence; see provider packet for retained receipt

blockers: Exact residential destination, degree audit and10–20-course nonduplicative applicability ledger remain unresolved.
Do not create mappings by course-title similarity.
findings.proposedAction: Watch and preserve existing mappings; no new residential pathway published.
